history.summary: This is a conserved Tiong Bahru heritage walk-up apartment on a 99-yr lease from 1967 — roughly 40 years of lease remaining and no en-bloc path due to URA conservation status. At $1.12M / $1,224 psf it carries severe financing limits (sub-60yr lease restricts LTV/CPF) and is a niche heritage product, not an investment vehicle.
history.rating_rationale: ~40-year remaining lease (1967 + 99yr) triggers low-lease financing constraints — limited LTV, restricted CPF use — and accelerating lease decay over a 5–7yr hold. Conservation status removes en-bloc upside, no URA comp data, score 301 (bottom decile). Buyer pool is heritage-niche owner-occupiers; this fails the investment liquidity and appreciation tests outright.
red_flags: ~40yr remaining lease — low-lease financing/CPF restrictions, steep decay
Conserved heritage walk-up — no en-bloc, niche buyer pool
No URA appreciation/comp data, score 301 (bottom decile)
catalysts: Tiong Bahru heritage charm — own-stay appeal only, not investment
